government.title: Bridging the Gap: A Qualitative Inquiry Into Misalignments Between Volunteer Management Practices and Volunteer Expectations
government.short_title: Bridging the Gap: A Qualitative Inquiry Into Misalignments Between Volunteer Management Practi…
government.plain_summary: This study explores how nonprofit managers and long-term volunteers have different expectations about their roles and experiences. Managers often focus on structure, standardization, and efficiency, while volunteers seek meaningful participation, emotional support, and autonomy. The research found significant misalignments across areas like onboarding, communication, task clarity, feedback, recognition, learning opportunities, scheduling flexibility, decision-making involvement, and relationships. These differences are not just operational but reflect broader tensions between formal systems and personal values.

government.title: Professional Data Use Among Nonprofits and Public Organizations in Collaborative Networks: The Influence of Partners, Coalitions, and Technical Assistance Organizations
government.short_title: Professional Data Use Among Nonprofits and Public Organizations in Collaborative Networks: The…
government.plain_summary: This study found that nonprofits and public organizations can improve their programs and decisions by using data from evaluations, especially when they work closely with similar organizations in partnerships. The research shows that the more an organization interacts with other similar groups within its own network of partnerships, the better it uses evaluation data for improvement. This means these organizations should focus on strengthening relationships within their specific networks to enhance how they use performance evaluation results.

government.title: Understanding Accountability in AI Use Within the Public Sector: Insights From State Governments in the United States
government.short_title: Understanding Accountability in AI Use Within the Public Sector: Insights From State Governmen…
government.plain_summary: This study examines how the public sector manages accountability in AI systems used by state governments. It found that accountability is crucial because it helps ensure AI systems are used fairly and transparently. The research also showed who is held accountable, what standards are used, and what the consequences are. It identified areas where more research is needed to connect theory with practice.

government.title: Blame Avoidance and Corruption: How Politicians' Denials Shape Citizen Perceptions and Political Accountability
government.short_title: Blame Avoidance and Corruption: How Politicians' Denials Shape Citizen Perceptions and Politic…
government.plain_summary: This study examines how politicians accused of corruption respond when they deny their wrongdoing. The research shows that when politicians say they are innocent or blame others for their actions, it can improve their image and chances of winning elections. This is especially true for people who strongly support one political party. Understanding this helps us see how leaders influence public opinion about corruption in politics.

government.title: Customer Experiences with Airline Refunds: An Analysis of Procedures, Challenges, and Policy Implications
government.short_title: Customer Experiences with Airline Refunds: An Analysis of Procedures, Challenges, and Policy I…
government.source: International Journal of Research in Entrepreneurship & Business Studies
government.plain_summary: This study analyzed how airlines handle airfare refunds and the challenges customers face during this process. It found that communication issues are a major problem, especially in understanding airline rules. Despite most customers being satisfied with their refund after receiving one, they felt the process was complex and inefficient. The research suggests clearer policies and better coordination between airlines, intermediaries, and customers could improve trust and service quality.

government.title: The Impact of Digital Technology on International Humanitarian Law: Ethical and Legal Implications of Autonomous Weapons Systems
government.short_title: The Impact of Digital Technology on International Humanitarian Law: Ethical and Legal Implicat…
government.source: European Journal of Law and Political Science
government.plain_summary: This article looks at how new technology like AI is changing international laws for wars. As weapons get more automated, it raises questions about who should be held responsible when they make decisions. The main idea is that current rules are still useful but need updating to fit with these new types of weapons. It suggests ways to improve the existing laws so that people in war zones can continue to rely on protections like not harming civilians unnecessarily.

government.title: Working Behavior Of Government Officials In Public Services In Dutuno Village, Paleleh District, Buol Regency
government.short_title: Working Behavior Of Government Officials In Public Services In Dutuno Village, Paleleh Distric…
government.plain_summary: This research looked at how government workers provide services in a village setting. They found that while the officials are polite to people, there are problems like being late or not responding quickly which affect how well they serve others. Showing care by helping with paperwork is good, but sometimes it takes too long and doesn't happen often enough. The biggest issue is following rules and showing up for work on time.

government.title: The concept ‘light from light’ in the Nicene creed: Is the metaphor still appropriate for Christian ethics today?
government.short_title: The concept ‘light from light’ in the Nicene creed: Is the metaphor still appropriate for Chri…
government.plain_summary: This article explores the concept 'light from light' found in early Christian texts like the Nicene Creed. It asks if this metaphor is still relevant for modern Christian ethics, especially considering new ways of thinking about Jesus and his divinity. The author suggests that understanding this ancient metaphor can help create a broader vision of what it means to be human and how we should act ethically today. They argue that by examining the historical context and biblical perspectives, we can find ways to apply these ideas in practical ways for modern ethical discussions.

government.short_title: Implementation of Anti-Corruption Villages Based on Local Wisdom: A Study in Banyubiru Village…
government.plain_summary: This study looked at how an anti-corruption program was implemented in Banyubiru Village near Semarang Regency using local customs and values like honesty, cooperation, and deliberation. The program worked well because it aligned with what people already believed in their community. Community members were actively involved in planning and overseeing the village budget. Local leaders also played a role by providing oversight and making sure things ran smoothly.

government.title: AI Regulation and Its Social Impacts on Public Policy
government.short_title: AI Regulation and Its Social Impacts on Public Policy
government.plain_summary: AI is now a key part of how governments make decisions in many areas like healthcare, policing, and welfare. As more AI systems are used, it's important to have rules to make sure they work fairly and don't cause problems. These rules help ensure that AI doesn't lead to unfair treatment or less democracy. By carefully watching how AI is used, we can make sure it helps people and doesn't hurt them.

government.title: Le facteur émotionnel de l’activité : analyser les « angles morts » pour améliorer la QVCT. Bilan d’une recherche immersive en Police Judiciaire française
government.short_title: Le facteur émotionnel de l’activité : analyser les « angles morts » pour améliorer la QVCT. Bi…
government.plain_summary: This research focuses on understanding the emotional risks in police work and how they manage their emotions to improve job satisfaction. It was conducted by observing various police units like forensic science, digital investigation, financial division, criminal division, anti-terrorism unit, and more over 26 days. The study found two key emotions that are hard for them to express: interest and frustration. These emotions make it difficult for officers to discuss their work-related feelings openly, leading to invisible or undiscussed labor.

government.title: Data Science as a Catalyst for Audit Transformation
government.short_title: Data Science as a Catalyst for Audit Transformation
government.plain_summary: Data science has become crucial as we generate vast amounts of information daily. It helps transform this data into useful insights for better decision-making across various sectors. For audit institutions, integrating data science can enhance their ability to manage public funds more effectively and improve accountability. By using data science, audits can provide clearer and more accurate reports that recommend improvements faster, which benefits the overall administration and improves citizens' quality of life.

government.title: Killer Robots – A Case for SAIs
government.short_title: Killer Robots – A Case for SAIs
government.plain_summary: This paper discusses a scenario where autonomous killer robots are used in warfare without human intervention. These robots can make decisions about who to target based on AI algorithms trained to recognize certain uniforms. If one of these drones targets and kills an enemy soldier who is surrendering, it would violate international laws. Another concern is if the robot makes a mistake by attacking another similar system, leading to unintended conflicts.

government.title: The dark side of public service motivation : Analysis of noble cause corruption based on the Lebanese case
government.short_title: The dark side of public service motivation : Analysis of noble cause corruption based on the L…
government.plain_summary: This study examines how public service motivation can lead to noble cause corruption in Lebanon, where there's a lot of social and economic hardship. The research found that feelings like compassion and selflessness often push people into doing good deeds for noble causes, but these actions sometimes involve corrupt practices. This leads to internal conflicts as the person feels both guilty and supported by their work environment. Factors like physical exchanges, personal space in the workplace, and close relationships with users can make it easier for this type of corruption to happen.

government.title: La face sombre de la motivation de service public : Analyse de la corruption pour une cause noble à partir du cas libanais
government.short_title: La face sombre de la motivation de service public : Analyse de la corruption pour une cause no…
government.plain_summary: This study examines how public service motivation can lead to corruption for a noble cause in Lebanon, where corruption is prevalent and social issues are challenging. Based on interviews with 32 Lebanese public servants, the research explores how feelings of compassion and self-sacrifice related to public service motivation might encourage them to engage in corrupt behavior for what they see as a good cause. The study highlights that these motivations can lead to behaviors like providing extra support or shielding users from punishment. This can create internal conflicts within the public servant due to their emotional connection with those affected.

government.title: CORRUPTION AND ACCOUNTABILITY ON THE PERFORMANCE OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT ADMINISTRATION IN NIGERIA: A CASE STUDY OF ILORIN-SOUTH
government.short_title: CORRUPTION AND ACCOUNTABILITY ON THE PERFORMANCE OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT ADMINISTRATION IN NIGERIA…
government.source: GOMBE JOURNAL OF ADMINISTRATION AND MANAGEMENT (GJAM)
government.plain_summary: This research examines how corruption affects local government performance in Ilorin-South, Nigeria. It found that practices like favoritism, ghost workers, and misusing funds significantly reduce the quality of services provided by these governments. The study also showed that having strong accountability measures such as audits, transparent reporting, and citizen oversight can improve service delivery. Overall, the research suggests that corruption deeply impacts local governance negatively, but implementing effective accountability systems can help improve efficiency and public trust in government services.

government.title: LEGAL BASIS OF ACQUITTAL IN BANKING CREDIT CORRUPTION: PANGKALPINANG DISTRICT COURT CASE
government.short_title: LEGAL BASIS OF ACQUITTAL IN BANKING CREDIT CORRUPTION: PANGKALPINANG DISTRICT COURT CASE
government.plain_summary: This research looks at how judges decided not to convict Ardian Hendri Prasetyo, who was accused of bank credit corruption at Bank Rakyat Indonesia in Pangkalpinang. The study found that while there were suspicions of misuse of power and financial loss, these weren't proven enough legally. This decision shows a preference for letting the person go when evidence is unclear or insufficient. It also emphasizes how important it is to interpret laws correctly in cases like this one involving banking corruption.

government.title: Evaluating the Effect of Corruption on Nigeria's Public Service Delivery
government.short_title: Evaluating the Effect of Corruption on Nigeria's Public Service Delivery
government.source: Innovative Research Journal of Sociology and Humanities
government.plain_summary: This study examines how corruption affects the delivery of public services in Nigeria. Despite efforts to combat it, corruption continues to hinder areas like infrastructure, healthcare, education, and civil administration. Corruption can manifest as inflated contracts, favoritism, bribery, or misuse of funds, which degrade service quality and widen inequality. The report highlights that its impact is particularly severe on vulnerable groups in rural areas and varies by region.

government.title: Instruments and Mechanisms of the European Union for Preventing and Combating Corruption
government.short_title: Instruments and Mechanisms of the European Union for Preventing and Combating Corruption
government.plain_summary: This article looks at how the European Union stops and fights against corruption. It covers tools like making information transparent and checking for conflicts of interest to prevent misuse of funds. There are special watchdogs like OLAF and the EU Court of Auditors who investigate issues and ensure proper use of money from the EU budget. A new body, EPPO, has been created to look into crimes that affect the EU's financial dealings.

government.title: Institutional Trust and Sector-Specific Corruption in Greece
government.short_title: Institutional Trust and Sector-Specific Corruption in Greece
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how different types of corruption affect people's trust in institutions in Greece. It found that public sector corruption often involves unclear rules and too much power for officials to make decisions. Private businesses sometimes bribe to get things done faster. The research also shows there are three main areas academics focus on: improving governance, understanding why people might cheat, and using technology like websites to be more transparent.

government.title: The Needs of Corruption Crimes Investigation and Main Directions of Forensic Research
government.short_title: The Needs of Corruption Crimes Investigation and Main Directions of Forensic Research
government.plain_summary: The paper discusses the challenges faced in preventing and investigating corruption crimes, highlighting how law enforcement is still not effective enough. Corruption involves various forms like bribery, embezzlement, and fraud, often using high-tech methods that can be repetitive and complex. To combat these effectively, we need advanced tools and strategies. The research suggests improving forensic techniques with modern digital methods to detect corrupt assets more efficiently.

government.title: Assessment of impact of technology innovation on procurement transparency in selected public sector in South-East Nigeria
government.short_title: Assessment of impact of technology innovation on procurement transparency in selected public s…
government.source: Journal of Commerce, Management, and Tourism Studies
government.plain_summary: This research looked at how technology affects the openness of buying things for government work in some areas of South-East Nigeria. They used surveys and picked participants randomly to understand better. The study found that using online ways to buy stuff helps make decisions more openly. So, they suggest governments should use these online methods to keep everything fair.

government.title: TRANSPARENCY, ACCOUNTABILITY, AND CORRUPTION RISK ASSESSMENT: CENTRAL BANK OF NIGERIA
government.short_title: TRANSPARENCY, ACCOUNTABILITY, AND CORRUPTION RISK ASSESSMENT: CENTRAL BANK OF NIGERIA
government.source: International Journal of African Research Sustainability Studies
government.plain_summary: This study on the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) looks at how transparently they operate under their laws. It found that without proper accountability measures in place, there can be issues like elite capture, misuse of funds, and financial mismanagement. These problems lead to a lack of public trust, higher inflation rates, and fewer foreign investments. The study recommends steps such as phasing out certain interventions, requiring independent audits, using digital methods for procurement, and targeting inflation to improve the CBN's credibility and reduce corruption risks.

government.title: Corruption in Public Procurement: From Definition towards a Case Study (Part II)
government.short_title: Corruption in Public Procurement: From Definition towards a Case Study (Part II)
government.plain_summary: This paper discusses how to prevent corruption in government buying things and services. It found that businesses often face issues like lack of transparency, dishonesty, and unfair competition when bidding on contracts. The third part looks at how one city handles these processes and suggests ways to make it easier for everyone while saving taxpayer money. By using new technology more, they could help reduce corruption and improve the process.

government.title: Gender-based variations in autogenous bone block graft availability within the mandibular ramus: a cone beam computed tomographic comparative analysis
government.short_title: Gender-based variations in autogenous bone block graft availability within the mandibular ramu…
government.source: International Journal Of Community Medicine And Public Health
government.plain_summary: This study looked at how much bone is available from the back part of the jaw (mandibular ramus) in different people based on their gender and age. They used special X-ray images to measure things like how thick the bone is, how dense it feels, and its overall volume. The results showed that men and women had similar amounts of usable bone, but as people get older, especially those over 40, the bone becomes less dense and thinner. This means healthcare providers need to consider a person's age when planning procedures like putting in dental implants or other surgeries that require bone grafts.

government.title: Public Sector Accounting and Accountability: a public value(s) perspective
government.short_title: Public Sector Accounting and Accountability: a public value(s) perspective
government.source: Accounting and Management Review | Revista de Contabilidade e Gestão
government.plain_summary: This article discusses how public sector accounting can be improved by viewing it through a lens of public value. Public value refers to what benefits society as a whole from government actions or programs. The study suggests that instead of just focusing on financial numbers, we should also consider the broader impact and benefits these services provide. By adopting this perspective, governments could better understand how their activities contribute to overall societal good.

government.title: Public Sector Accounting and Accountability: a public value(s) perspective
government.short_title: Public Sector Accounting and Accountability: a public value(s) perspective
government.source: Accounting and Management Review | Revista de Contabilidade e Gestão
government.plain_summary: Public sector accounting often focuses on measuring, controlling, reporting, and managing public value. This article suggests a new way to look at how public sector accounting can be improved by viewing it through the lens of public value. By adopting this perspective, practices might become more aligned with what citizens expect from their government services. This could lead to better decision-making that benefits society as a whole.

government.title: ETHICS AND LEGAL FRAMEWORK OF PUBLIC RELATIONS VISUAL COMMUNICATION AS A MEDIA OF PUBLIC EDUCATION IN ENCOURAGING SUSTAINABLE GLOBAL ECONOMIC RECOVERY IN THE ERA OF DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION
government.short_title: ETHICS AND LEGAL FRAMEWORK OF PUBLIC RELATIONS VISUAL COMMUNICATION AS A MEDIA OF PUBLIC EDUCA…
government.source: International Journal of Law Government and Communication
government.plain_summary: Digital transformations have made using visuals an important part of how Public Relations communicates information. This helps educate people about things like sustainable economic recovery. But with more use of digital visuals comes new rules and ethical standards to follow. Our research looked at these issues, finding that following good ethics and staying within legal guidelines is key for effective PR communication.

government.title: AN ECONOMIC ANALYSIS OF OECD ANTI-CORRUPTION INSTRUMENTS AND THEIR INFLUENCE ON PUBLIC SECTOR PERFORMANCE AND REGULATORY QUALITY IN KAZAKHSTAN
government.short_title: AN ECONOMIC ANALYSIS OF OECD ANTI-CORRUPTION INSTRUMENTS AND THEIR INFLUENCE ON PUBLIC SECTOR…
government.plain_summary: This study examines how implementing OECD anti-corruption standards affects public sector performance and regulatory quality in Kazakhstan. It found that stronger institutions and better regulations are linked with more foreign direct investment, lower transaction costs, and modest economic growth. The research also shows that full implementation of these standards can lead to significant improvements, but partial adoption is a barrier. Understanding this relationship helps policymakers design effective anti-corruption strategies for improving the economy in Kazakhstan.

government.title: Research on the Impact of Blockchain-Based Credible Return Information Mechanism on the Anti-Fraud Effect of Government Subsidies
government.short_title: Research on the Impact of Blockchain-Based Credible Return Information Mechanism on the Anti-F…
government.source: International Journal of Global Economics and Management
government.plain_summary: This research looks at how a blockchain-based system can help prevent fraud when governments give out subsidies. Currently, some people cheat by pretending they're getting refunds on subsidized items but don't actually send the money back. The study suggests creating an honest return information system where all transactions are recorded in a transparent ledger. This way, everyone involved—from e-commerce sites to government auditors—can see if returns happen as promised.

government.title: Data Transparency as a Tool for Accountability: Norwegian Municipalities’ Approaches to Elderly Care Information, and Broader Implications
government.short_title: Data Transparency as a Tool for Accountability: Norwegian Municipalities’ Approaches to Elderl…
government.plain_summary: This study examines how Norwegian municipalities handle requests for information about accidents involving elderly people. It found that while Norway is known for having a free press, citizens still have limited access to data related to elderly care. The research shows some municipalities are not fully compliant with sharing this type of sensitive information under the Freedom of Information Act. This highlights a need to improve transparency in elderly care services to ensure better quality and accountability.

government.title: Seek and hide: Retention of lenient auditors in the anti-corruption campaign in China
government.short_title: Seek and hide: Retention of lenient auditors in the anti-corruption campaign in China
government.plain_summary: This research looks at how state-owned enterprises in China keep their regular accountants after a big anti-corruption push started in 2012. It found that companies with lenient auditors are less likely to switch from their current accountants during this time. This suggests they might be trying to hide any signs of corruption. The study also shows that companies with more extravagant spending, weaker ways of running themselves, and smaller or not specialized accountants tend to keep these lenient auditors even more.

government.title: Effectiveness of a comprehensive bystander anti-racism intervention for healthcare staff in Australia
government.short_title: Effectiveness of a comprehensive bystander anti-racism intervention for healthcare staff in Au…
government.plain_summary: This study looked at how training healthcare workers on recognizing and responding to racism worked over time. It found that after participating, staff understood more about racism's effects and felt better equipped to handle racist incidents. They also reported feeling supported by their workplace in dealing with such situations. The training was well-received by most participants who thought it useful and would recommend it to others.

government.title: Favoritism Practices, Nepotism, and Corruption in Public Administration: Impacts on Employment, Meritocracy, Efficiency, and Institutional Trust. An Institutional and Governance Perspective in Transitional Public Sectors
government.short_title: Favoritism Practices, Nepotism, and Corruption in Public Administration: Impacts on Employment…
government.source: European Journal of Management, Economics and Business
government.plain_summary: This study looks at favoritism, nepotism, and corruption in the public administration of Kosovo. It shows these practices hurt merit-based hiring, reduce efficiency, and decrease trust in government by families and clans influencing decisions. The research also found that this leads to lower employee motivation and performance, unfair recruitment and promotion processes, and less confidence from citizens. These issues can slow economic growth because they discourage foreign investment and innovation.

government.title: The Challenges of Backsourcing
government.short_title: The Challenges of Backsourcing
government.plain_summary: The challenges of backoutsourcing in the public sector can be significant due to legal requirements, limited options for service providers, and interdependencies with existing contractors. These factors often lead to informal agreements or "silent contracts" between authorities and service providers to maintain continuity without formal termination processes. This can result in opportunistic behavior and less oversight compared to formal contracts. Understanding these complexities is crucial for public sector managers who need to plan more proactively to avoid such issues.

government.plain_summary: This research looks at how election results can be tampered with during vote counting, which could make election outcomes unfair. In Indonesia, manipulating votes is against the law and can result in legal consequences. The government has set up a center to handle these issues by combining different agencies like Bawaslu (Election Supervisory Body), Police, and Prosecutor's Office. To prevent this from happening again, it’s important for all involved parties to be professional and honest.

government.title: Who Acts, and Who is Watched? Differences Between Top-down and Bottom-up AI Anti-Corruption Tool Implementation Methods
government.short_title: Who Acts, and Who is Watched? Differences Between Top-down and Bottom-up AI Anti-Corruption To…
government.plain_summary: This research looks at how governments use artificial intelligence (AI) to fight corruption in two ways: top-down and bottom-up. Top-down methods involve government agencies using AI, which can make the process more efficient but might create a cycle where corruption is harder to detect. Bottom-up approaches let citizens participate more directly through AI tools, but they face challenges like limited access to open data. The study suggests that both methods have pros and cons, and there's a need for better integration of citizen participation with AI technology to effectively combat corruption.

government.title: Governing Money Laundering as a Collective-Action Problem: The European Anti-Money Laundering Authority (AMLA)
government.short_title: Governing Money Laundering as a Collective-Action Problem: The European Anti-Money Laundering…
government.plain_summary: Money laundering is a significant threat affecting competitive markets, security, and consumer well-being. The European Anti-Money Laundering Authority (AMLA) was created as part of new EU regulations to improve supervisory standards and coordinate the fight against illicit finance across Europe. AMLA combines classification functions like setting rules and standards with selective enforcement tools such as direct supervision of high-risk groups and escalation mechanisms. By viewing these aspects through a collective-action lens, it helps explain how AMLA can effectively police money laundering while also highlighting its limitations in fully addressing the issue.

government.source: Journal of Information, Communication and Ethics in Society
government.plain_summary: This study aims to create a framework that helps ensure ethics are considered when people from different backgrounds collaborate on creating policies or services for the public sector. The research found it's crucial to have an ethical guide at the beginning of such projects, as issues can vary based on what service is being created and where it’s happening. This work is important because current rules don't cover all aspects of public sector co-creation, so having a flexible ethics framework is needed to address these unique situations effectively.

government.short_title: Conditions of benefits and risks when algorithmic technology is implemented for public sector…
government.plain_summary: This study examines how artificial intelligence is used in police work and for catching scams, looking at both good things it can do and problems it might cause. Many places are using AI now because they think it will make their jobs better. But sometimes these tools have caused big issues. The research found that while people who build the technology focus on what's good about it, those studying government work look more at the risks.

government.title: Media freedom and government budget transparency in Africa
government.short_title: Media freedom and government budget transparency in Africa
government.source: Journal of Information, Communication and Ethics in Society
government.plain_summary: This research looks at how much freedom there is for news organizations in African countries and whether this affects how transparent governments are with their spending. The study found that more press freedom leads to better government financial disclosures, but only up to a point—once it reaches about 52 out of 100 on a scale measuring media freedom. Beyond this level, additional press freedom doesn't improve transparency further. For policymakers, the key takeaway is that fostering a certain amount of free press can help governments be more open with their finances, but they need to ensure the press remains relatively independent and not too powerful.

It found that people can sometimes connect what they think with what's really happening. People also tend to see more corruption when the governor from their party isn't in power. The research shows that knowing a lot about politics doesn't change these perceptions much.

government.source: Transforming Government: People, Process and Policy
government.plain_summary: This study investigates how certain organizational factors impact the successful implementation of Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems in New Zealand's government agencies. It found that leadership commitment, organizational preparedness, user capability development, and change management readiness are crucial for ERP success. Leadership support was identified as the strongest predictor of ERP deployment success. Interestingly, cultural differences did not significantly affect ERP outcomes.

government.title: Does municipal ownership ensure accounting quality? The role of corruption in accounting manipulation
government.short_title: Does municipal ownership ensure accounting quality? The role of corruption in accounting manip…
government.source: International Journal of Public Sector Management
government.plain_summary: This study examines how municipal ownership affects the quality of financial reporting in Italian municipalities. It found that having more of an enterprise owned by the municipality is linked to lower chances of manipulating financial reports, suggesting stronger oversight from local government. However, if those owning the municipality have a history of corruption, this reduces the effectiveness of municipal ownership in preventing manipulation. Essentially, for municipal ownership to be effective, the people running these municipalities need to act with integrity and not engage in corrupt practices.

government.short_title: The Anti‐Fraud Lever: China's Strategic Use of the Scam Crackdown to Invigorate the LMLECC Pro…
government.plain_summary: China took strong action against fraud rings targeting Chinese citizens, especially those using telecommunications and the internet. This included joint operations with other countries and high-profile actions by officials like Liu Zhongyi. While this helped reduce major fraud centers, it strained relations between China and Thailand due to how China handled things. This shows that fighting crime can be used as a way for China to exert more influence in the region.

government.title: Measuring and assessing corruption in public health systems in low- and middle-income countries: a scoping review of methods
government.short_title: Measuring and assessing corruption in public health systems in low- and middle-income countrie…
government.plain_summary: Corruption in public health systems can severely affect healthcare outcomes and fairness. Different ways exist to measure this corruption, but they haven't been well studied together yet. This review looked at various methods used globally, especially in low- and middle-income countries. Common tools include surveys, interviews, focus groups, and audits.

government.title: Hunting Tigers or Swatting Flies? The Impact of Anti-corruption Information in China
government.short_title: Hunting Tigers or Swatting Flies? The Impact of Anti-corruption Information in China
government.plain_summary: This study examines how different types of anti-corruption information affect public perceptions of corruption across different levels of government in China. It found that information about local anti-corruption efforts, like "swatting flies," reduces perceptions of corruption at lower levels but doesn't have a clear effect at higher levels. On the other hand, information about high-profile cases like "hunting tigers" impacts people who are more sensitive to corruption. The study suggests that anti-corruption campaigns should be tailored to different levels of government and individual attitudes towards corruption for better effectiveness.

government.plain_summary: This study looked at how using special techniques like forensic interviews and tracking money movements can help stop fraud in the way public pension systems manage their funds. The research found that when these methods are used more often, there is less fraud happening. This was seen both by looking at numbers and talking to people who run these systems. Using these techniques seems to make it harder for bad guys to cheat the system.

government.title: The Challenges of Implementing E-government in the Public Sector: A Case Study on The Gambia
government.short_title: The Challenges of Implementing E-government in the Public Sector: A Case Study on The Gambia
government.plain_summary: E-government has become a way for governments to deliver services more efficiently and make governance transparent. However, implementing it can be challenging, especially in developing countries with limited resources. A case study from The Gambia found that while e-government helps improve service delivery, transparency, accountability, and citizen participation, there are still big hurdles like not having enough IT infrastructure or skilled employees to use digital tools effectively. There's also a lack of collaboration between different government departments and issues related to internet access and trust in government services.

government.source: Lex localis - Journal of Local Self-Government
government.plain_summary: Governments are increasingly using AI to improve services like citizen assistance, compliance checks, fraud detection, and planning. These systems can significantly speed up response times and save time for workers. However, without proper oversight, AI can undermine accountability by making decisions harder to understand or challenge, especially in developing countries where institutions might not be fully developed. To address this, a practical risk-based governance model has been proposed.

nonprofit.short_title: Bridging the Gap: A Qualitative Inquiry Into Misalignments Between Volunteer Management Practi…
nonprofit.plain_summary: This study explores how nonprofit managers and long-term volunteers have different expectations about their roles and experiences. Managers often focus on structure, standardization, and efficiency, while volunteers seek meaningful participation, emotional support, and autonomy. The research found significant misalignments across areas like onboarding, communication, task clarity, feedback, recognition, learning opportunities, scheduling flexibility, decision-making involvement, and relationships. These differences are not just operational but reflect broader tensions between formal systems and personal values.

nonprofit.title: Professional Data Use Among Nonprofits and Public Organizations in Collaborative Networks: The Influence of Partners, Coalitions, and Technical Assistance Organizations
nonprofit.short_title: Professional Data Use Among Nonprofits and Public Organizations in Collaborative Networks: The…
nonprofit.plain_summary: This study found that nonprofits and public organizations can improve their programs and decisions by using data from evaluations, especially when they work closely with similar organizations in partnerships. The research shows that the more an organization interacts with other similar groups within its own network of partnerships, the better it uses evaluation data for improvement. This means these organizations should focus on strengthening relationships within their specific networks to enhance how they use performance evaluation results.

nonprofit.short_title: Customer Experiences with Airline Refunds: An Analysis of Procedures, Challenges, and Policy I…
nonprofit.source: International Journal of Research in Entrepreneurship & Business Studies
nonprofit.plain_summary: This study analyzed how airlines handle airfare refunds and the challenges customers face during this process. It found that communication issues are a major problem, especially in understanding airline rules. Despite most customers being satisfied with their refund after receiving one, they felt the process was complex and inefficient. The research suggests clearer policies and better coordination between airlines, intermediaries, and customers could improve trust and service quality.

nonprofit.title: Recent Expansions in Anti-Microbial Profile of Quinoline Analogues: A Review
nonprofit.short_title: Recent Expansions in Anti-Microbial Profile of Quinoline Analogues: A Review
nonprofit.plain_summary: Recent research has shown that adding different parts called heterocyclic systems to quinoline molecules can create compounds with many useful properties. These modified quinoline-based drugs are effective against a wide range of harmful bacteria, including those causing serious infections. They also show promise in treating cancer and other conditions like seizures, pain, inflammation, and heart problems. By combining quinoline with other parts, scientists can make new medicines that work better than existing ones.

Corruption can manifest as inflated contracts, favoritism, bribery, or misuse of funds, which degrade service quality and widen inequality. The report highlights that its impact is particularly severe on vulnerable groups in rural areas and varies by region.

This helps educate people about things like sustainable economic recovery. But with more use of digital visuals comes new rules and ethical standards to follow. Our research looked at these issues, finding that following good ethics and staying within legal guidelines is key for effective PR communication.

nonprofit.short_title: Effectiveness of a comprehensive bystander anti-racism intervention for healthcare staff in Au…
nonprofit.plain_summary: This study looked at how training healthcare workers on recognizing and responding to racism worked over time. It found that after participating, staff understood more about racism's effects and felt better equipped to handle racist incidents. They also reported feeling supported by their workplace in dealing with such situations. The training was well-received by most participants who thought it useful and would recommend it to others.

nonprofit.short_title: Beyond Compliance: A Systematic Review of Ethics, Accountability, And Transparency in Indonesi…
nonprofit.plain_summary: This study looks at how ethics, accountability, and transparency work together in Indonesian government systems. It found that even with digitalization efforts, if there isn't a strong enough foundation of ethics, these measures can fail to prevent corruption and lose public trust. The research suggests integrating ethical practices, making information transparent, and ensuring accountability are all important for effective governance. By combining these elements, Indonesia can improve its government systems and build more trustworthy relationships with the people it serves.

nonprofit.title: CHALLENGES AND DIRECTIONS FOR IMPROVING THE EFFECTIVENESS OF UKRAINE’S STATE ANTI-CORRUPTION BODIES
nonprofit.short_title: CHALLENGES AND DIRECTIONS FOR IMPROVING THE EFFECTIVENESS OF UKRAINE’S STATE ANTI-CORRUPTION B…
nonprofit.plain_summary: This article discusses key issues facing Ukraine's anti-corruption bodies and suggests ways to improve their effectiveness. Challenges include fragmented legal support, political instability, lack of coordination among agencies, limited resources, unclear jurisdictional powers, and low public trust. To address these, the Ukrainian government should focus on strengthening institutional independence, optimizing power distribution, improving human resources, enhancing coordination mechanisms, and increasing transparency in sensitive areas like procurement and financial controls. These steps are crucial for building trust with society and aligning anti-corruption efforts with European standards of governance.

nonprofit.short_title: Working Paper 57: Mapping and strengthening the evidence base for anti-corruption Collective A…

nonprofit.plain_summary: This working paper offers a new way to understand how different groups like businesses, non-profits, and governments can work together more effectively against corruption. It includes tools that help researchers, practitioners, and policymakers compare various anti-corruption efforts and see what works best in different places. By understanding how these collaborations impact real-world changes in preventing corruption, it helps design better partnerships to make a difference. This paper is supported by Siemens and comes from the Basel Institute on Governance.
